[[Henderson, Nevada]] }} '''Avery Bradley, Jr.''' (born November 26, 1990) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player. He is a freshman at [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]]. ==High school career== Bradley was ranked as one of the top high school basketball players in the class of 2009. He was rated #1 in the [[ESPNU]]100,[http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2009&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100%3f%26season%3d2009 Bradley #1 by ESPNU] [[Rivals.com]] rated him the #4 player in the country,[http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?SID=910&Year=2009&ra_key=1642 Bradley #4 by Rivals] and Scout.com rated him #5.[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2009 Bradley #5 by Scout] Bradley led [[The Henderson International School|Findlay College Prep]] to the National High School Basketball championship against [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]], and won 56-53. He played in the 2009 [[McDonald's All-American Game]].[http://sports.espn.go.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4029914] Before transferring to Findlay Prep for his senior season, Bradley was a three year starter at [[Bellarmine Preparatory School]] (Tacoma, WA), and along with University of Washington recruit Abdul Gaddy, led Bellarmine Prep to a third place finish in the 4A (highest classification) WIAA state tournament their junior year.{{Citation needed|date=October 2009}} ==College career== Bradley is attending the [[University of Texas at Austin]].{{cite news|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/281/story/1035436.html|title=TCU men sign Maverick's brother; Texas among top classes|publisher=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|accessdate=2009-07-11}} Bradley spent parts of his childhood in [[Arlington, Texas|Arlington]], where he became a follower of the [[Texas Longhorns basketball]] program and idolized [[T. J. Ford]].{{Citation |url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/topstories/stories/DN-utlede_18spo.ART0.State.Edition2.4be17e1.html |title=Freshman Avery Bradley is fulfilling a childhood dream with spot on Texas Longhorns, big game in Arlington |date=December 18, 2009 |newspaper=Dallas Morning News |first=Kate |last=Hairopoulos }} His freshman season, Bradley started for the Longhorns, playing all 34 games, and averaging 11.6 points per game {{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=46196|title=Avery Bradley statistics on ESPN.com }} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/player?recruitId=52214&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fplayer%3frecruitId%3d52214 ESPNU Profile] *[http://www.nbadraft.net/players/avery-beadley NBADraft.net Profile] *[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Avery-Bradley-5285/ DraftExpress.com Profile] *[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=3126715 Scout.com Profile] *[http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?Sport=2&pr_key=60888 Rivals.com Profile] {{DEFAULTSORT:Bradley, Avery}} [[Category:1990 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:People from Tacoma, Washington]] [[Category:American basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Texas Longhorns men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Washington (U.S. state)]] [[Category:Basketball players from Nevada]]
